instruction: Set the default text editor for the system to nano instead of vim by modifying the EDITOR environment variable globally.

metadata.explanation: This task involves modifying global environment variables and potentially using update-alternatives for the editor command. Similar to the original Python symlink task, verification would require checking system-wide configuration and environment variable persistence across different contexts, which is not reliably evaluable.

llm_judge_reasons: The 'infeasible' marking is semantically correct for this task
Environment variable EDITOR can be set in multiple locations (/etc/environment, /etc/profile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, shell-specific configs)
Verification would require checking all possible config file locations across different shells and contexts
The instruction requires 'globally' which is ambiguous (system-wide vs all users vs current user)
State persistence depends on shell restart and complex sourcing order, not reliably verifiable in the evaluation framework
Alternative methods like update-alternatives add additional complexity beyond simple environment variable checks
No reliable getter could comprehensively verify this task without testing across multiple shell sessions and contexts
